operators.name: custom_max_dim1
semantics: Computes torch.max(x, dim=1) exactly: returns a named tuple (values, indices) where values is the maximum over the channel dimension and indices is the corresponding argmax (int64).
The reduction is over dimension 1 (channels) of the 4-D input tensor of shape [B, C, H, W].
Output values and indices have shape [B, H, W], preserving broadcasting semantics.

The input tensor must be on CUDA and of dtype torch.float32, but may have any strides; the kernel handles non-contiguous layouts or can force contiguity internally if needed. The output tensors are allocated contiguous on CUDA.
The function must return a torch.return_types.max container, which is constructed by wrapping the two output tensors; no torch computation is allowed inside the operator.

operators.name: custom_stack_dim1
semantics: Computes torch.stack((x, x), dim=1): copies the input tensor twice along the new dimension 1 (after batch dimension) to create a 5-D tensor of shape [B, 2, C, H, W].
The two stacked copies are identical to the input; output[ :, 0, ...] = x and output[ :, 1, ...] = x.

The input tensor is of dtype torch.float32 on CUDA, any strides are allowed. The output must be contiguous with stride layout [2*C*H*W, C*H*W, H*W, W, 1] (assuming continuous dimensions; the actual function should allocate contiguous memory and place data accordingly).
This operator performs only memory movement/copy, no arithmetic. It is a custom CUDA kernel that can take advantage of coalesced writes.
The output tensor must preserve the data of the input for both slices along the new dimension.
Compute the maximum value along the channel dimension (dim=1) of the input tensor x of shape [512, 8, 256, 256].
The result is a named tuple (values, indices), where values is a torch.float32 tensor of shape [512, 256, 256] and indices is a torch.int64 tensor of shape [512, 256, 256].
The indices part is discarded (_) in the reference, but debug_forward must yield the complete tuple including indices.
The operation is performed on CUDA, and the output tensors must have contiguous strides as specified.
Stack the input tensor with itself along a new dimension 1 to create a tensor of shape [512, 2, 8, 256, 256].
Both slices are identical copies of x: x_stacked[:,0] == x and x_stacked[:,1] == x.
The operation has no numerical computation; it only reorganizes memory.
The output tensor is of dtype torch.float32, on CUDA, and must be contiguous.
Return a Python tuple containing x_max (the tensor of max values from step_001) and x_stacked (the stacked tensor from step_002).
The tuple's first element is a torch.float32 tensor of shape [512, 256, 256], and the second is a torch.float32 tensor of shape [512, 2, 8, 256, 256].
Both tensors are on CUDA.
